messages.subject: #Rscript.bat in batchfiles 0-7.1 ~ Why can't I get it to work?
parts:
Following the instructions here:

https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/sqldf/rscript/sqldf/t3sfmb0kPUw/cVcFJESpfdgJ

I have copied the contents of 'R.bat' into a new file called '#Rscript.bat' in the same location.

Using the Redmond Untility I have added the batchfiles 0-7.1 directory to my Windows path. It looks like this:

Variable name: PATH
Variable value: C:\R\batchfiles_0.7-1; [other stuff]

However, running a file called "test.bat" with the contents

#Rscript %0 %*
print(pi)

I get the error

C:\R>test
C:\R>#Rscript test
The system cannot find the path specified.

Which makes me think that "#Rscript.bat" is not recognised on the windows path.

Advice would be much appreciated.

Regards,
Ynot

O/S: Windows Server 2008 R2
R-3.2.2

#Rscript %0 %*

Your test.bat script works for me so it may be that #Rscript.bat is not on your path as you suggest.  Try this from the Windows cmd line:

     where #Rscript.bat

If it responds that it can't find it then #Rscript.bat is not on your path.  Note that you do not have to put all of the batchfiles on your path -- you only need to put #Rscript.bat on your path.  The files in batchfiles, including #Rscript.bat, are each self contained and none depends on any other file.

If you issue this command from the Windows cmd line:

    path

it will give you your path so just put #Rscript.bat in one of those directories.

I have created a new script. 

1. Download it from:

     https://batchfiles.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/%23Rscript2.bat 

2. rename it to #Rscript2.bat

3. You will have to edit the file to set the R_HOME variable (and you may have to set the R_ARCH variable) as discussed in the file.

More instructions are at the top of the file itself.

The idea is that while its not completely authormic like #Rscript.bat it is very simple so if anything goes wrong it should be easier to diagnose the problem.
